dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Things are already enough of a mess as it is. Tsaritsa preserve us, please don‘t let it snow now...

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Me? Sobolev. I’m the engineering supervisor here. Anything related to ice mining becomes my headache. Though "supervisor" might be giving me too much credit. I'm really just a slightly higher-ranking laborer...

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Judging by the way you're dressed, you must be a traveler from out of town. If you need help, you can ask Nekrasov in town. Handling visitors and answering questions is his job.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Heh, though I doubt there's much that fellow will actually help you with. If you run into real trouble, you'll have to fend for yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Nothing good, that's for sure. The biggest problem is the drop in temperature. Not only does the ice-mining equipment start breaking down, but the workers can't take it either.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: And if heavy snow blocks the roads, the trains will have to stop running. At that point, never mind delivering our cargo on time. We may not even be able to get the supplies and parts the town urgently needs.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Still, we’ve already made every preparation we can in advance. All that's left to do now... is pray, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, do you need a hand with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Funny you should ask. I've got a shipment that needs to be loaded up and sent off to Snezhnograd soon. Problem is, three people from the escort team still haven't shown up.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: We could probably manage without the three of them, but if anything goes wrong on the road and we suddenly find ourselves short-handed, that'll be a real headache.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: My guess is those fools got the date wrong, and they're probably still down below with their heads buried in work. Sorry to trouble you, but could you make a trip over to their work area and look for them?

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Hmm. Looks like those three fools managed to make it onto the transport. Thank goodness... So long as they didn't hold anything up, giving them grief over it's more trouble than it's worth.

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: Thanks for making the trip. At least one thing finally got sorted out today... Oh, right. Here's your payment. Thanks for the help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Sobolev
dialogues.text: No... *sigh* I'm afraid the only notable thing is my work being a notable mess...
